metadata.title: Example Sensor Gateway System Security Plan (draft)

system-characteristics.description: The system gives the installation security operations center (SOC) a near-real-time picture of perimeter intrusion and environmental conditions (temperature, flooding, power loss) at remote sites . It senses and forwards only: it makes no decisions and actuates nothing, and operators act on alarms through other systems . The program is in engineering and manufacturing development; twelve pre-production units at test sites feed a test instance of IODS, and 60 units are to be fielded after an authorization decision .

information-types.title: Perimeter and environmental sensor telemetry and alarms
information-types.description: Intrusion, door, temperature, water and power readings and alarms with site and sensor identifiers, collected from the field sensor network and forwarded to IODS.

availability-impact.adjustment-justification: An outage removes sensing at one site; the SOC compensates with guard patrols for several days, so the provisional low value is kept.

information-types.title: ESG configuration and security management data
information-types.description: Device configuration, host firewall rules, account records and cryptographic keys of the gateway.

confidentiality-impact.adjustment-justification: The data includes private keys and firewall rules whose disclosure would let an attacker impersonate a gateway or map the permitted paths into the enclave.

information-types.title: ESG audit records
information-types.description: Sign-in, account change, privilege use, configuration change and update events.

authorization-boundary.description: One gateway appliance per site with its operating system, collector service, admin console and buffer database, plus the field sensor nodes paired with it, authorized as one system across all sites on one configuration baseline. The installation network switch port is the boundary edge. IODS, the installation ICAM service, the installation network enclave and the CSSP are outside the boundary and separately authorized; technician laptops and administrator workstations are installation assets outside the boundary.

network-architecture.description: Each gateway has three interfaces. The uplink port on the enclave VLAN permits outbound TLS 1.3 to IODS, outbound syslog over TLS to the CSSP collector and inbound HTTPS to the console from the installation management VLAN only; the host firewall denies all other traffic in both directions. The maintenance port is disabled unless a technician enables it with the shelter key switch, serves only the console over HTTPS on a link-local address, and has no routing to the uplink. The field radio is an encrypted, paired link to the sensor nodes, which have no IP connectivity. The enclave firewall in front of every site switch enforces the same permitted flows.

data-flow.description: DF-1 sensor node to collector over the paired encrypted radio, unpaired nodes and malformed messages rejected; DF-2 collector to buffer, local on the encrypted data partition; DF-3 collector to IODS over TLS 1.3 with mutual certificate authentication; DF-4 audit records from the gateway to the CSSP SIEM over syslog with TLS; DF-5 administrator workstation to console over HTTPS with sign-in through the identity service; DF-6 console to identity service over TLS with signed assertions; DF-7 on-site technician laptop to console over HTTPS on the maintenance port with local sign-in. DF-3 to DF-6 cross the boundary edge and DF-7 enters through the maintenance port.

components.title: ESG gateway appliance
components.description: Ruggedized fanless appliance with uplink and maintenance Ethernet ports and a field radio module, in a locked alarmed shelter

components.title: Gateway operating system
components.description: Hardened Linux-based OS image with host firewall (deny by default) and local audit daemon

components.title: Sensor collector service
components.description: Receives and validates sensor messages from the field radio, writes them to the buffer and forwards them to IODS

components.title: Admin web console
components.description: HTTPS console for configuration, accounts, diagnostics and update upload

components.title: Local buffer database
components.description: Embedded database holding up to 7 days of telemetry while IODS is unreachable

components.title: Field sensor network
components.description: Up to 40 battery-powered sensor nodes per site and their firmware, paired to the site gateway by radio

components.title: Installation Operations Data Service
components.description: Receives ESG telemetry (IC-1) under an interconnection agreement signed 2026-04-02; separately authorized, ATO to 2029-03-15

components.title: Installation ICAM Service
components.description: Installation identity provider; DoD PKI authentication and account workflow for remote ESG administrators and auditors; covered by the enclave authorization

components.title: Installation Network Enclave
components.description: Enclave firewall, intrusion detection and network access control in front of every ESG; separately authorized

components.title: Installation Cybersecurity Service Provider
components.description: SIEM log collection and correlation, monitoring and incident response for the installation; separately authorized

inventory-items.description: Ruggedized fanless gateway appliance with uplink and maintenance Ethernet ports and a field radio module; one per site

control-implementation.description: Planned and implemented controls for baseline SP800-53B-MODERATE-SUBSET-6.

by-components.description: Implemented today: (a) the console allows only identity-service accounts mapped by group claim to the admin or auditor role, one break-glass local account (esgadmin) and the shared local fieldtech account; no other account type is permitted. (b) The ISSO is the ESG account manager. (c, d, e, i) A remote user files an ESG access request that the ISSO approves; the installation identity service's account workflow then creates the account and its group membership, which sets the user's role and privileges on CMP-WEBUI. (f, h, l) When a user leaves or changes role, the identity service disables the account or removes the group claim, which ends console access; the ISSO confirms removal at the next review. (g) Sign-in, account-change and privilege-use events from CMP-WEBUI and CMP-GW-OS go to the CSSP SIEM, and the ISSO reads the ESG report weekly. (j) The ISSO reviews the console account list against the access request records quarterly; the last review is dated 2026-09-12. Break-glass use is logged and reported, and its credential is sealed in the program office safe. Missing: the shared fieldtech account used by about 10 field technicians on the maintenance port cannot be attributed to an individual, and (k) its shared password is changed every 90 days rather than when a technician leaves the group. Plan: per-technician local accounts with smart-card login in software release 2.3, planned for 2027-03; until then on-site privileged actions are not individually accountable.

(a) The OS audit daemon on CMP-GW-OS, the collector (CMP-COLLECTOR) and the console (CMP-WEBUI) are able to log sign-in success and failure, account changes, privilege use, configuration changes, update installation, service start and stop, and radio pairing events. (b) The program coordinated the event list with the Installation Cybersecurity Service Provider, which agreed it on 2026-05-20 so that it feeds the CSSP's SIEM correlation; the CSSP collects and correlates the forwarded events, and that part is inherited. (c) All of these event types are logged continuously on every unit and forwarded over TLS to the SIEM within one minute, with 30 days held locally. (d) The ISSE's rationale: the list records who signed in, who changed accounts, configuration or firewall rules, what software was installed, whether a service was stopped, and whether a sensor was paired, which is what an after-the-fact investigation of an ESG incident needs. Events from the shared fieldtech account name the account, not a person; that weakness is tracked under ac-2. (e) The ISSO and the CSSP review and update the event list annually. The system's own part is event generation and forwarding on its three components; the ISSO reads the ESG-specific SIEM report weekly.

values: DISA SRGs and STIGs applicable to each component

by-components.description: (a) The configuration settings for CMP-GW-OS, CMP-COLLECTOR, CMP-WEBUI and CMP-STORE are the DISA SRGs and STIGs applicable to each component: the developer builds one signed OS image from the General Purpose Operating System SRG and the applicable application and web server guidance, in the most restrictive mode consistent with the mission. (b) The build pipeline applies the hardening settings, and every unit runs the same signed image. (c) The pipeline records each deviation from the guidance, and the RSSPO configuration control board approves deviations and any change to the baseline; the approved deviations are listed in the program's STIG summary. (d) A configuration check runs nightly on each unit and reports drift from the approved baseline to the CSSP SIEM; the 2026-09-30 witnessed SRG/STIG scan found the approved baseline on all 12 units and no drift in August or September 2026.

Implemented today: remote administrators and auditors are uniquely identified and authenticated by the Installation ICAM Service with their DoD PKI smart card; the ICAM service issues the identities, validates the credential and asserts the identity and group claim, and that part is inherited. On CMP-WEBUI the system configures the federation, maps the group claim to the admin or auditor role, refuses any user without an approved claim (DT-2 passed), and runs every console session and action under the asserted identity, so audit events name the person. The break-glass account esgadmin is a single named account, sealed in the program office safe, with each use logged and reported. Local sign-ins lock for 30 minutes after five failures and sessions lock after 15 minutes idle (both passed in DT-2). Missing: about 10 field technicians sign in on the maintenance port with the shared local fieldtech account and a shared password, so they are not uniquely identified and processes started in those sessions are associated with the shared account, not a person. The ICAM service covers no local accounts. Plan: per-technician local accounts with smart-card login that works without the identity service, in software release 2.3, planned for 2027-03.

(a) The external managed interface is the uplink port of CMP-GW-HW to the site switch. The host firewall on CMP-GW-OS denies all traffic by default and permits by exception only outbound TLS 1.3 to IODS on one port, outbound syslog over TLS to the CSSP collector, and inbound HTTPS to the console from the installation management VLAN. The key internal managed interfaces are the maintenance port, which is disabled until a technician enables it with the shelter key switch, serves only the console on a link-local address and has no routing to the uplink, and the field radio, a paired encrypted link over which sensor nodes have no IP path to the uplink. Firewall rule changes are logged and approved by the configuration control board with the baseline. DT-2 port scans from the installation network and the maintenance port found only the documented ports and no routing between ports. (b) ESG has no publicly accessible components, so no separate subnetwork is needed. (c) Each unit connects to other systems only through the site switch on its own enclave VLAN, behind the enclave firewall, intrusion detection and network access control of the Installation Network Enclave, which permits at the enclave edge only the registered flows; that part is inherited under the enclave ATO of 2025-11-20. The system's own part is the host firewall and port design on its two components, and notifying the enclave before any new flow.

values: 30 days from release of the update bundle

by-components.description: Implemented today: (a) the developer identifies flaws in the OS, collector, console and database (CMP-GW-OS, CMP-COLLECTOR, CMP-WEBUI, CMP-STORE) from vendor advisories and its own scans and corrects them in a signed monthly update bundle; monthly vulnerability scans and the bundle level of each unit are reported by the ISSO to the ISSM, and units past the remediation period are reported to the program office. (b) Each bundle is built by the baseline pipeline and regression-tested on the pre-production units before release, and each unit verifies the bundle signature before installing it. (d) Each bundle is a baseline change approved by the RSSPO configuration control board, and the nightly configuration check confirms the installed level. Missing: (c) security-relevant updates are not installed within 30 days from release of the update bundle on fielded units, because bundles are installed only during quarterly site visits while remote update over the installation network is not approved. At the 2026-09-30 scan, esg-north-01 and esg-ridge-01 ran the 2026-07 bundle, 63 days old, with 4 high and 9 medium vulnerabilities fixed in later bundles; the other 10 units were current with no findings. Plan: remote update over the uplink in software release 2.2, planned for 2026-12; until then each unit past 30 days is tracked in a POA&M item as the organizational rule requires.
